text.p: U.S. stocks were lower in morning trading on Friday with Wall Street still burdened by concern over Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning on the market's heights, and by weakness in technology shares.

Traders said a market-friendly revision to fourth quarter gross domestic product data was not enough to cheer bonds or stocks. The Dow was down about 21 points, or 0.3 percent, at 6904 after dipping to an early low of 6883.
The Nasdaq composite, studded with tech stocks, was off nine points, or 0.7 percent, at 1303. The long bond dipped 4/32 to yield 6.81 percent.
